dossier.public_summary: The 15-day 19730-ppm dip alternates deep and shallow every orbit (9492 vs 23490 ppm) and shows a negative secondary eclipse almost half as deep as the primary at phase 0.27. Depth also varies by ~100% between sectors and between the 5 individual transits, which are mostly caught near a data gap. This varying odd-even and secondary signal matches an eclipsing binary, not a 5.5-Earth-radius planet on a quiet host.

reasons.why: Alternating odd/even transits differ by 60% (ratio 2.5) with 3.2 sigma significance (sector_oe_max_sigma 3.057), indicating two different eclipse depths on adjacent 15-d cycles. No planet explanation; typical of eclipsing binary at twice the period.

Significant secondary eclipse ~44% as deep as the primary near phase 0.27 (secondary_over_bump 1.548 vs best brightening), well above brightening noise, with roughly half the dip's depth - inconsistent with a small planet and positively indicating a stellar eclipsing binary.
reasons.value: snr 4.915 phase 0.2678 depth_ppm 8657 best_brightening_snr 3.176 depth_over_dip 0.4387 secondary_phase_offset 0.2322 secondary_over_bump 1.548

reasons.why: Depth changes by ~100% between sectors and between individual transits (p_consistent 1.99e-05), with most signal from the top 3 of 5 transits and many transits near a data gap. Changes_within_a_source shows even QLP depths differ, so not a pipeline calibration offset but intrinsic variability of eclipses, supporting a binary/blend rather than a stable planet.

reasons.why: Large out-of-eclipse swing at the 15-d period (ratio_to_depth 0.154, chi2 28.06/9) together with very large spot modulation (rotation amplitude 26k-27k ppm) shows the signal is caught in highly variable light, typical for an eclipsing binary or blend diluted by M-dwarf activity, not a quiet planet transit.
